videos.title: The #1 Lie You’ve Been Told About Exercise (Do THIS Instead) | Dr. Shannon Ritchey
videos.description:
Hard workouts might be why your body isn’t changing...

In this episode, Dr. Shannon Ritchey and Jay Shetty bust the fitness myths that keep you stuck. Shannon is a physical therapist. At 24, she worked out hard every day and felt like she was 90. Then she cut her workouts almost in half and got in the best shape of her life.

She shares the simple test that tells you if a set really counted. She explains why being sore isn’t proof your workout worked. And Jay asks her why eating more protein made him bigger, not leaner.

Learn why cardio barely moves the scale, and the four rules Shannon says will build muscle for almost anyone.

videos.title: How to Rewire Your Brain to Crave Healthy Foods
videos.description:
Dr. Scott Kanoski, PhD, is a Professor of Human and Evolutionary Biology and Neurobiology at the University of Southern California. 

We discuss how different foods impact memory and cognitive function as well as cravings. 

We also discuss how GLP-1 drugs work to control hunger in the brain and body, the role of the gut microbiome, and the effects of artificial and low calorie sweeteners on hunger and satiety. 

This episode highlights how nutrition impacts much brain health and learning capacity and how our memory impacts food choices too.

videos.title: Is Failure Really Your Best Teacher?
videos.description:
80,000 Hours: Go to https://80000hours.org/solved to get your free copy of their career guide and start planning a career that is meaningful.
Momentous: Head to https://livemomentous.com and use code SOLVED for up to 35% off your entire first order.

You've heard a hundred failure stories by now. Notice anything? Almost every one is told by someone who succeeded. Drew and I open the failure episode with a Silicon Valley conference built entirely around founders sharing their biggest flops, and why it...failed. We also get into the WWII bomber study that led the military to armor the wrong parts of its planes, and why today's straight-A students are often the most terrified of failing. If failure is supposed to be something to celebrate, why does it feel scarier than ever?
Get your free episode guide: https://mrk.mn/failureguide

This is just CHAPTER 1 of our episode on Failure. New chapters drop every week, but the FULL episode is available NOW: https://youtu.be/OEKLtP4fj1I
